target.title: refactor: centralize bounded file reads in fs-safe
target.body:
Related: #110594
Related: #110591
Related: #110592
Related: #110516
Related: openclaw/fs-safe#41
Related: openclaw/fs-safe#43
Related: openclaw/fs-safe#44

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw owned duplicate asynchronous and synchronous loops for allocation-bounded reads from file descriptors that had already been opened and pinned by a filesystem boundary. That duplicated policy now owned by fs-safe and made the byte-limit/error contract easier for the two implementations to drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes all eight descriptor-read consumers through the existing boundary-file facade and delegates incremental reads to the published fs-safe advanced API. The facade preserves OpenClaw's established RangeError message for oversized files, while the duplicate 63-line reader is deleted. The eighth caller is the exec-approvals file reader that landed on main while this PR was under review; rebasing brought it under the same shared boundary.

The dependency is pinned to @openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.4. OpenClaw's downstream EPERM fsync patch and patch allowlist entry are removed because that compatibility fix now ships upstream. Both lockfiles and the Plugin SDK API baseline are regenerated from the published artifact, and the package-patch test fixture no longer treats the removed fs-safe patch as approved.

Downstream exact-head proof caught two upstream compatibility regressions before this could land:

- fs-safe PR #43 restored the pre-0.4.2 regular-file overflow message without losing bounded allocation behavior.
- fs-safe PR #44 restored OpenClaw's opt-in dead-owner sidecar-lock recovery with an exclusive reclaim guard. Default recovery remains fail-closed; explicitly configured recovery is serialized so one reclaimer cannot delete a fresh replacement lock.

Exact-head hosted CI then caught a stale downstream timeout test double: the production path correctly switched from FileHandle.readFile() to fs-safe's incremental FileHandle.read(), but the test still mocked the old method and therefore no longer stalled. The test now mocks the actual bounded-read seam and its timeout behavior is covered again.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible behavior change. Config input, secrets plans, exec-approvals files, agent message files, local avatars, hook metadata, and workspace bootstrap files retain their existing size limits and overflow messages while sharing fs-safe's allocation-bounded implementation. Session, registry, and Plugin SDK locks retain their configured dead-owner recovery behavior without restoring the unsafe compare-then-unlink race.

## Evidence

- Published dependency: [@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.4](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openclaw/fs-safe/v/0.4.4), [GitHub Release](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.4.4), integrity sha512-QklFGshaQDXl7RFyxPeSN/1moYq/X+SJcmX/nY3oXJO/tzVasL9i1g3m4nJqIfd6qUTJQjeu+41aIqw8+SbUww==.
- fs-safe PR #44 passed the Node 22/24 Linux/macOS/Windows matrix, coverage, benchmarks, build, workflow lint, file-size guard, and filesystem-boundary guard. [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/29674875128), [coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/29674875142), [benchmarks](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/29674875130).
- OpenClaw head 2d2c8e68aa6b8: a fresh Blacksmith Testbox accepted the frozen lockfile, installed the published 0.4.4 package, and passed 161 tests across the bounded-read integration files plus every Plugin SDK, session, and sandbox-registry stale-lock surface that failed on 0.4.3.
- OpenClaw head 2d2c8e68aa6b8: full pnpm build passed, including CLI bootstrap imports, Plugin SDK exports, runtime postbuild, and Control UI budgets.
- OpenClaw head 15fca373ff3c1: full pnpm check:changed passed on a fresh Blacksmith Testbox in 8m40s, including all shrinkwrap guards, the full TypeScript project graph, every Oxlint shard, regenerated Plugin SDK contracts, patch/database guards, and runtime import cycles.
- Exact OpenClaw head f0d7562950c886e5169678567038f8430c53b14e: a fresh Testbox frozen install passed all 34 secrets resolver tests after correcting the stale timeout test double. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29676872311) passed the bounded-read/runtime lanes; its only first-attempt failure was a checkout infrastructure error, which was rerun.
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview was clean before the metadata-only 0.4.4 bump. The pnpm and npm dependency records were then reviewed separately with no findings because the scanner treats the public registry digest as credential-shaped; the actual digest was restored and matched byte-for-byte against npm. The generated-baseline review and final timeout-test repair review were also clean.
- git diff --check passed.

fs-safe PR #39 remains a separate guarded-mkdir API-design discussion and is intentionally not part of this dependency update.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation, dependency source/API, generated artifacts, and test evidence.
